**Agents can ask you for a credential from a card in the app, the lead's chat shows compaction as it happens and asks before re-sending an expired context, agents' branches are named after their work, finished agents clean themselves up, the lead and the agents get separate default models, agents set up and test much faster, and every agent has an animated avatar.**

## What's new

- **Credential requests.** When something fails on auth, an agent can ask you for what it lacks: a
  GitHub account that can reach the repository, or a secret by name. You answer from a
  **Credential** card in the project's chat, the agent's thread in the rail, or the agent's own
  chat: pick or log in a GitHub account, type the secret, or refuse. The value goes from the app to
  the daemon and into the agent's machine, never through a model's conversation.
- **Compaction you can see.** When the lead's chat compacts, a live card shows it happening, and it
  runs in the background instead of holding up your next message.
- **No surprise re-sends.** Before a message would re-send a lead context whose prompt cache has
  expired, or is about to, the chat asks you: **Compact and send**, or **Send anyway**.
- **Branches named after the work.** A new agent's branch is named from the slug you give it, or
  from its title or task, like `agentbox/csv-export`, instead of `agentbox/agent-12`.
- **Pull requests found by their commits.** An agent's pull request shows in the rail, in
  `list_agents` and in finish notices whatever branch it was pushed to.
- **Finished agents clean themselves up.** The daemon removes an agent whose pull request was
  merged or closed, or that finished more than a day ago with no changes and no pull request. It
  never removes one that's busy, has uncommitted work, or has commits that exist nowhere else, and
  it keeps a branch only when there's work on it. Media is kept for as long as the new **Media
  retention** setting says (a day by default), in Settings → Agents or with
  `agentbox media retention`.
- **Separate defaults for the lead and the agents.** Settings has a **Lead** tab beside **Agents**,
  each with its own default model and context window (200k or 1M).
- **Accounts.** Rename a Claude Code account (Settings, or `agentbox auth claude rename`) or a
  GitHub account, and every project and agent using it follows. A new project allows only the
  Claude Code account it was created with, and a project's GitHub picker lists every GitHub
  account again.
- **Faster agents.** Agents' temporary files go to a tmpfs, archives unpack faster, and
  `agentbox image build --dev-caches` fills the Go, npm and Electron caches for agents working on
  AgentBox itself. The desktop tools answer each action with a screenshot taken once the screen has
  settled, which cuts a typical click-and-check from dozens of steps to a few, and agents now test
  and show UI through the desktop first.
- **Animated avatars.** Each AI tool's agents have a small animated character that acts out what
  the agent is doing.
- **Smaller things.** A **New project** button in the sidebar's Projects header; clearer wording for
  what the per-agent resource limits mean; a running agent picks up the daemon's new `agentbox`
  binary when the daemon starts, instead of keeping the old one until its machine restarts.

## Fixes

- **Windows' WSL setup card no longer flickers** on first launch while the daemon can't be reached
  yet. It did in 0.1.0.
- **A project's GitHub account picker lists every account.** In 0.1.0, a project that limited its
  Claude Code accounts only listed GitHub accounts named like one of them.
- **Agents' pull requests show again**, however their branch is named. In 0.1.0 they only showed
  when the pull request's branch was the agent's own.

|---|---|
| `AgentBox-0.2.0-x86_64.AppImage` | The desktop app, with the `agentbox` command-line tool inside — runs on any Linux distribution |
| `AgentBox-0.2.0-amd64.deb` | The desktop app, for Debian and Ubuntu (`sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.2.0-amd64.deb`) |

## Install

```bash
chmod +x AgentBox-0.2.0-x86_64.AppImage
./AgentBox-0.2.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

Or, on Debian/Ubuntu, `sudo apt install ./AgentBox-0.2.0-amd64.deb`; on Arch, `sudo pacman -U
AgentBox-0.2.0-x64.pacman`. On a Mac, open the `.dmg` and drag AgentBox into Applications, then see
**Known limitations** below. On Windows, run the installer or the portable `.exe`. See the README's
[Install](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/blob/v0.2.0/README.md#install) for the rest.

**Upgrading from 0.1.0:** the agents' base image changed, so Settings asks you to rebuild it
(`agentbox image build`). Agents made before the rebuild keep working on the old image.

## Known limitations

- **The Mac app is alpha, and ad hoc signed.** There's no Apple signing certificate yet, so macOS
  refuses to open it the first time: after that first failed launch, choose **Open Anyway** in
  **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, or clear the quarantine with
  `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AgentBox.app`. This ad hoc signed build hasn't yet
  been confirmed to launch on a real Mac; if it doesn't on yours, please
  [report it](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/issues).
- The rest are unchanged since
  [0.1.0](https://github.com/leciric/agentbox/releases/tag/v0.1.0): Windows is
  alpha too, and there's no SECURITY.md yet.
